title: Acid-Catalyzed Degradation of Murexide: An Accessible Experimental and Computational Approach
content: Acid-catalyzed degradation limits the stability of many organic molecules, and its study often requires advanced instruments. This study shows how cyclic voltammetry, UV-vis spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, available in most laboratories, can be combined to study such reactions, using murexide as a model system. The degradation of murexide, measured by the decrease in its cyclic voltammetric peak current, followed pseudo-first-order kinetics. The apparent rate constants were 0.0058, 0.0119, and 0.0343 min⁻¹, with half-lives of 119, 58, and 20 min at pH 4.9, 3.0, and 2.0, respectively. The UV-vis rate constant at pH 4.9 agreed with the electrochemical value. The large peak separation (730–742 mV) indicated slow electron transfer at the Pt electrode, with a transfer coefficient (α) of 0.32 and a heterogeneous electron transfer rate constant (k⁰) of (5.2 ± 0.2) × 10⁻4 cm s⁻¹. DFT calculations showed that protonation at the C5 carbon (calculated pKa ≈ 3.1) opens a low-energy hydrolysis pathway to alloxan and uramil. TDDFT analysis showed that the loss of the absorption at 510 nm is due to dis-ruption of the C5–N–C5 conjugation. This combined approach provides an accessible framework for studying acid-catalyzed degradation in research and teaching settings.
